summary: Naga Airport (WNP/RPUN) is a medium-sized domestic airport serving Naga City, the economic hub of the Bicol Region in the southeastern Philippines. Located in the province of Camarines Sur on Luzon island, it provides essential air access to the region, connecting it with Manila and other Philippine destinations. The airport supports both commercial passenger flights and general aviation operations in this predominantly agricultural and pilgrimage-oriented area.
faqs:
Q: How far is Naga Airport from Naga City center?
A: The airport is conveniently located within the city, approximately a short drive from the central business district and major landmarks.

Q: What airlines operate from Naga Airport?
A: Several Philippine domestic carriers serve this airport, offering regular flights primarily to and from Manila.

Q: Does Naga Airport have international flights?
A: No, Naga Airport currently handles domestic flights only, with passengers connecting through Manila for international travel.

Q: What facilities are available at the terminal?
A: The terminal offers standard amenities including check-in counters, waiting areas, restrooms, and basic food and beverage concessions.
transport_tips: Tricycles and jeepneys are commonly available outside the terminal for short trips into Naga City and surrounding areas. Pre-arranged private car transfers or hotel shuttles are recommended for visitors unfamiliar with local transport. Travel time to central Naga is typically brief, making the airport a convenient gateway to the Bicol Region.
local_tip: Time your visit to explore the nearby Peñafrancia Festival if traveling in September—Naga hosts one of the largest religious pilgrimages in the Philippines, celebrated in honor of Our Lady of Peñafrancia, the patroness of the Bicol Region.
